Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

{
 "path": "programs/task-412ce0d5.py",
 "content": "def transform(grid):
    """Keep first-panel foreground cells where the aligned second panel is background."""
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])

    # Locate the full-height/full-width separator.
    split_col = next((c for c in range(w) if len(set(row[c] for row in grid)) == 1), None)
    split_row = next((r for r in range(h) if len(set(grid[r])) == 1), None)
    if split_col is not None and (split_row is None or w - 1 > h - 1):
        left = [row[:split_col] for row in grid]
        right = [row[split_col + 1:] for row in grid]
    elif split_row is not None:
        left = grid[:split_row]
        right = grid[split_row + 1:]
    else:
        raise ValueError('No full separator found')

    assert len(left) == len(right) and len(left[0]) == len(right[0])
    # Background is the most frequent color on the second panel.
    from collections import Counter
    counts = Counter(v for row in right for v in row)
    background = counts.most_common(1)[0][0]
    return [[3 if a != background and b == background else background
             for a, b in zip(row_a, row_b)]
            for row_a, row_b in zip(left, right)]
"
}

{
 "path": "programs/task-412ce0d5.py",
 "content": "def transform(grid):
    """Mark cells where the two aligned panels contain the same color."""
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    vertical = [c for c in range(w)
                if len({grid[r][c] for r in range(h)}) == 1
                and c == w - 1 - c]
    horizontal = [r for r in range(h)
                  if len(set(grid[r])) == 1 and r == h - 1 - r]

    if vertical:
        c = vertical[0]
        left = [row[:c] for row in grid]
        right = [row[c + 1:] for row in grid]
        assert all(len(a) == len(b) for a, b in zip(left, right))
    elif horizontal:
        r = horizontal[0]
        left, right = grid[:r], grid[r + 1:]
        assert len(left) == len(right)
    else:
        raise ValueError("No centered full-length separator found")

    return [[3 if a == b else 4 for a, b in zip(row_a, row_b)]
            for row_a, row_b in zip(left, right)]
"
}
